Not required, and nothing went wrong. That wall of text is the command's actual product in its default mode, and it's the optional half of what the command does.

`entire runner setup -y` does two separate things (`cmd/entire/cli/runner_setup.go:92`):

1. **Scaffolds `.entire/runners/*.json`** — the six default runners (`trail-risk`, `-confidence`, `-drift`, `-security`, `-review`, `-summary`). This is the part enablement needs, and it already happened before the wall printed. Check `ls .entire/runners/` — if you have six files, you're enabled. Commit them.
2. **Prints a tailoring prompt to stdout** — because you didn't pass `--run`. It gathers repo signal (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/README capped at 6k/6k/2k chars, top-level dirs, recent merged PRs and issues via `gh`, checkpoint churn hotspots, past trail findings) and embeds it plus all six current runner templates into one prompt meant to be pasted into your agent. That's tens of thousands of characters, hence the wall.

The shipped templates are generic (written for a web/backend app — payments, DB migrations), so step 2 rewords their scored dimensions for your repo. **The defaults are functional without it** — `runner_setup.go:264` explicitly reports un-tailored runners as "functional as-is". Two lines on stderr at the very bottom say the same thing, but they're easy to miss after that much scrollback.

Ways to skip the wall:

```bash
# The prompt goes to stdout; the human status lines go to stderr.
entire runner setup -y > /tmp/runner-prompt.txt

# Or do the tailoring headlessly via your configured summary provider —
# prints only "updated <file>" lines instead of the prompt.
entire runner setup -y --run
```

Re-running is safe either way: it no-ops on scaffolding once the files exist (`runner_init.go:27`) and asks before re-tuning.

One thing worth fixing on the docs side: the instructions give `-y` without saying the default mode dumps a paste-ready prompt, which is exactly why it reads as a failure. Want me to file an issue against the enablement doc, or propose wording — either `--run`, or the redirect, plus a note that the defaults work untailored?
but is it also writing them without "--run" ?

Yes. The scaffolding write is unconditional — `--run` only controls the *tailoring* half.

`runRunnerSetup` calls `ensureRunnersPresent` at `cmd/entire/cli/runner_setup.go:107`, before it ever looks at `opts.run`. The `!opts.run` branch that prints the prompt is at line 138. So:

| | files created | templates rewritten |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setup -y` | yes (6 defaults, if none existed) | no — prompt printed for you to paste |
| `setup -y --run` | yes (same) | yes — in place, via your summary provider |

`-y` is precisely what authorizes that write without the confirmation prompt (`runner_init.go:41` — without it and without a TTY, it refuses: *"no runner configs found under …; re-run with --yes to create the default set"*).

So `git status` in that repo should show six untracked `.entire/runners/trail-*.json`. Those are the enablement artifact; commit them and you're done. The wall of text changed nothing on disk.

Two edge cases: the write only fires when the directory had no `*.json` at all (`runnerConfigsExist`, `runner_init.go:28` — it's a no-op otherwise, not a merge), and if runners *did* already exist, `setup -y` with no `--run` writes nothing and, on a non-TTY, just prints `Runners already configured. Re-run with --run to tailor them headlessly.`

Yes — exactly the six embedded defaults, byte-for-byte, with no model involvement.

They come from a `go:embed` in `cmd/entire/cli/runnerdefaults` (`runners/*.json`), and `ensureRunnersPresent` writes `f.Data` straight through (`runner_init.go:58`). Nothing is generated, merged, or repo-derived at that step. Total 6.8 KB across the six files:

| file | bytes |
| --- | --- |
| `trail-confidence.json` | 1125 |
| `trail-drift.json` | 1094 |
| `trail-review.json` | 1548 |
| `trail-risk.json` | 1077 |
| `trail-security.json` | 1119 |
| `trail-summary.json` | 881 |

Each is mostly structural config — `runtime` (agent, timeout, sandbox), `automation`, `select.trigger_types`, `output` (adapter, result type, monitor key/label/polarity) — plus a deliberately minimal prompt template. `trail-risk`'s whole template is four lines: role, `git diff origin/{{base_branch}}...HEAD`, score 0–100, output-JSON contract.

That split is the design: the embedded structural contract is always valid (so a runner can actually launch and its output parses), while the templates are short on purpose because tailoring is what fills in the repo's real dimensions and score bands. So after `setup -y` you have six working-but-generic evaluators — a risk score anchored to nothing in particular rather than to your repo's actual failure modes.

One consequence worth knowing: the templates you get must keep their `{{placeholder}}` set (`{{branch}}`, `{{base_branch}}`, plus `{{previous_findings}}` for review), because `validateNewTemplate` rejects a tailoring that adds or drops one. So if you later hand-edit them, don't remove a placeholder or `setup --run` will refuse to tune that runner.

content.text:
Your mapping is the right one, and the current flags are inverted from it. Concretely what's wrong today:

**`--run` is the flag that makes the command finish its job.** Without it, `setup` scaffolds and then stops, emitting a request for someone else to do the other half. A default mode should be the complete action, not the half one.

**`-y` doesn't answer every question the command asks.** `runner_setup.go:126` never consults `opts.assumeYes` — it only reaches `ensureRunnersPresent`. So on a repo that already has runners, `setup -y` still asks the re-tune confirm in a TTY, and on a non-TTY prints `Re-run with --run to tailor them headlessly`. `-y` means "yes to everything" everywhere else; here it means "yes to one of the two prompts". That's a defect on its own, independent of any redesign.

**`--run` also doubles as a confirmation bypass** — line 132's comment says "`--run` is taken as an explicit yes". So two flags both mean "don't ask me", with different scopes.

**And there's no `--dry-run`**; the closest thing is the default, which is why it surprises.

Mapped onto your sketch:

| | today | your model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setup` (TTY) | confirm *create defaults?*, then dump prompt | one question: defaults only, or defaults + adapt? |
| `setup -y` | scaffold, dump prompt, no adaptation | scaffold + adapt |
| `setup --dry-run` | — | adapt, show the diff, write nothing |
| `setup --run` | scaffold + adapt | (gone; `-y` is this) |

One genuine decision inside "preview of adapted": it can mean *run the model and show the resulting diff without writing* (a true dry-run, costs a provider call), or *show the prompt* (cheap, but it's a preview of the request, not of the adaptation). Those are two different features and I'd keep both — `--dry-run` for the first, and today's behaviour behind an explicit `--print-prompt`, so nobody gets 40 KB unless they typed its name.

Second consideration: making `-y` adapt means it now makes a provider call and can fail on provider config, where today it's local and free. Every provider except the external-plugin path implements `GenerateText` (claudecode, codex, copilotcli, cursor, geminicli, pi), so that failure is rare — but a CI/scripted enablement path may still want scaffold-only, which argues for a `--defaults-only` escape hatch.

Worth doing now specifically because runners are still internal-only: the population that would notice a flag-semantics change is a handful of Entire repos, so it's cheap today and won't be once this is customer-facing.

Want me to implement it, or write it up as an issue first? And separately — the `-y`-doesn't-answer-the-second-prompt bug is a small standalone fix if you'd rather land that ahead of the redesign.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

## [0.10.5] - 2026-09-03

### Changed

- Mirror creation goes through the control plane's async request routes by default, reporting queued, placing, and cloning progress instead of holding one request open for the whole placement; the `async_mirror_requests` setting it shipped behind in 0.10.4 now defaults on. Opt out with `"async_mirror_requests": false`. In async mode `--wait-timeout` is one deadline across submission, placement, and clone readiness, not clone readiness alone ([#2246](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2246))
- Entire no longer installs a `Read(./.entire/metadata/**)` deny rule into Claude Code's or Factory Droid's permission config, so agents in auto mode stop prompting for permission on ordinary commands. A deny rule is a hard block auto mode's classifier cannot get past, and it matched on the path being named rather than on anything being read, so a recursive grep from the repo root needed hand approval. `entire enable` clears one an older CLI left behind and `entire doctor` repairs it ([#2258](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2258))
- `entire experts --repo <owner>/<repo>` takes the repo id from the placement lookup that already chose its cell, and now tells "not onboarded" apart from "processing placement failed or suspended" instead of guessing at three causes ([#2222](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2222))

### Fixed

- A session's `full.jsonl` is released from `.entire/metadata` once its content has been condensed into a checkpoint. Nothing ever emptied that staging buffer, so transcripts accumulated in the worktree forever after being committed and pushed — 460 MB across 392 session directories in one checkout. Existing files are not reclaimed automatically ([#2258](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2258))
- `git clone entire://<cluster>/…` works again when your active login is on a different federation and exactly one saved login can authenticate that cluster; the CLI uses it and names it on stderr. `--context` and `$ENTIRE_CONTEXT` are unchanged ([#2248](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2248))
- `entire doctor` says it is waiting for a session lock instead of stalling with no output ([#2232](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2232))

Implemented. `entire runner setup` now has one decision point instead of two half-answered ones.

**The new surface**

| | behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `setup` (TTY) | asks once: *create the defaults and tailor them* / *create the generic defaults only* |
| `setup -y` | creates the defaults if missing, then tailors them — the full action |
| `setup --defaults-only` | creates the generic defaults and stops; no provider call |
| `setup --print-prompt` | the old default: creates as needed, prints the prompt for your own agent |
| `setup --dry-run` | tailors and shows a diff, writes **nothing** — not even the defaults |
| `setup --run` | deprecated alias for `-y`, hidden from help, warns |

`--defaults-only`, `--print-prompt` and `--dry-run` are mutually exclusive; an explicit mode outranks `-y`, so `-y --dry-run` still writes nothing.

**What that fixed**
